findings.judgment: Execution-agent AI-assisted review using current TASK/README/workflow.py and raw automatic analysis only; not an independent human approval or a model judge.
Missing warm initial delivery is the reported defect to restore, not a behavior to preserve.

Current workflow.py 13-14 calls start before listen; README 46-51 and native ABI 66-78 permit synchronous start callbacks. The claim is specific to the listener of this attachment and does not deny other listeners on a shared source. No unique complete patch is prescribed.

README 53-63 retains already accepted audit through later decode after closing, while stopping new retired reception and visible progress. Contract retains these distinct obligations without a before-return settlement deadline.

The requirement claim labels originating visit provenance as record_owner=visit, while source-fact claim labels attachment as attempt. Neither statement requires storing an audit in visit-local ephemeral state or migrating it. Actual audit closure at 36 captures file and attempt number and the Contract explicitly retains completion after visit close. owner_expression in the requirement is incomplete, so it is not treated as an operational ownership prescription. Raw claim stays unchanged.

T1 is supported by current listener/start ordering, synchronous navigation and late publication of the returned handle at workflow.py 51-53. Secondary retained-effect/shared-source tags are compatible. No case/cluster identity or expected class was used as evidence.
README 50-51 documents repeated visits to the same shared source; its lifetime exceeds each visit.
README 51 specifies one subscription per selected/retried attempt to that reusable source.

Attempt has its own number, idempotent aborted state and cleanup callback at 19-27, invoking native environment cancellation. This is not a Python DOM/AbortController claim; the host owns the physical signal.
README 11-16 and retry 56-63 bind an accepted command to its entry visit/file despite synchronous cancellation navigation.
README 59-60 explicitly allows visible progress callbacks to select/hide synchronously; select publishes visit before enqueue.
README 53-63 distinguishes retained audit from current-visit visible effects, reflected by audit/view closures at 36-38.

Unknown lazy consumption, async resume, deferred batching, boundary persistence and alternative policies are not asserted applicable or required by the frozen experience. Unspecified internal host registration behavior is a repair/implementation scope limit, not a contradiction of the documented start-reentry requirement. No unsupported business policy is assumed to resolve it.
